items.title: 4.1.7.1 Operations on Tree (Insertion, Deletion, Traversal: In-order, Pre-order, Post-order; Searching)

source_refs.note: Topic 4.1.7.1 Operations on Tree (PDF 109-111, printed 106-108). The promised insertion code is missing. Figure 4.8 mirrors 2 and 3 relative to the traversals; the original diagram follows the text. MCQ 7 is answered (b); the key gives (d). Long question 6 is answered. Recorded.

items: Insertion: find the right place and connect the new node to its parent, like adding a family member.
Deletion: remove a node carefully so the rest of the tree stays connected.
Traversal: visit every node in a set order: in-order, pre-order or post-order.
Searching: go through the tree checking nodes until the one wanted is found.

blocks.caption: Traversals of the tree with root 1, children 2 and 3, and leaves 4, 5, 6, 7

blocks.alt: Left: a binary tree with root 1, children 2 and 3, and leaves 4, 5, 6, 7, labelled root, edge, leaves and height 2, with BFS, in-order, pre-order and post-order sequences. Top right: a family tree with Grandparent, Parent1, Parent2 and Child1, Child2 under Parent1. Bottom right: an AVL tree with root 20, left child 15 having children 10 and 18, and right child 30.
blocks.caption: Tree terms, traversals, a family tree and an AVL tree (original diagram after topics 4.1.5 to 4.1.7).
blocks.long_description: In the binary tree, 1 is the root, 4 to 7 are leaves, and the height is 2 edges. Breadth-first order is 1 to 7 level by level; in-order visits left subtree, root, right subtree: 4, 2, 5, 1, 6, 3, 7; pre-order visits the root first: 1, 2, 4, 5, 3, 6, 7; post-order visits the root last: 4, 5, 2, 6, 7, 3, 1. The family tree has Grandparent at the root with two parents, and Parent1 has two children. In the AVL tree the left subtree under 15 has height 1 and the right subtree 30 has height 0, so they differ by only 1 and the tree is balanced.
